notes: SHIP v1.14.430 - THE COLOUR GOES IN THE ACCENT, NOT THE FILL. A SAME-DAY CORRECTION TO .429. WHAT .429 GOT WRONG. .429 routed the flat elevation through the one vocabulary, which was right, and then painted the bay colours into background on body.rd .rack-canvas-block, which was wrong. Those selectors carry three classes plus an attribute and therefore OUTRANK the dark tray base directly above them, so in the redesign house every classified device rendered as a SOLID SATURATED SLAB. That is precisely the defect the .229 comment sitting four lines away records about .228 - the ghost-fix over-filled to a solid slab that drowned the label - and the redesign design for these blocks is a DARK tray body plus a thin type-colour LEFT accent, which is a ruling rather than a default. I read the base rules, the ruling and the two disagreeing palettes, and still put the colour in the wrong channel. HOW IT WAS CAUGHT. Not by eye and not on device. The served-bytes check after pushing .429 counted TWO matches for a selector that should have appeared once, which surfaced a pre-existing body.rd border-left-color block keyed on the SAME display names. Reading that block is what exposed both the source-order conflict and, one line above it, the dark-tray ruling the backgrounds were breaking. A count that did not match the expectation was the whole tell. THE FIX. The .429 background rules are removed outright. The colours move into the border-left accent where the design puts them, and the bay stays canonical: pdu is pulled OUT of the cooling group and takes the bay gold - cdu maps to pdu in _TMAP - storage moves gold to the bay pink, server moves slate to the bay light blue, and gpu and switch take the bay exact hex rather than the near-miss --cyan and --violet. cooling, fan, crah and crac keep green: a different channel, never in dispute. patch, media and unknown stay grey per the standing 2026-08-06 ruling, stated explicitly rather than reaching the default accent by accident. Coverage is unchanged at 8 of 11 - the routing from .429 was never the problem. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. The Vocabulary door, the idempotence guarantee, and the Rule 17 gate on rackElevation_buildHtml all shipped correctly in .429 and are untouched here. ?legacy=1 still emits the raw code and still matches only the non-house-scoped base rules. TESTS: spec 20 now asserts the ACCENT rather than the fill, and adds the guard .429 needed and did not have - every classified block must keep the dark tray body, so putting a channel colour back into background fails immediately. 20 plus 06-composition: 18 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4585/4585, CRLF 57051 with 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep. DEVICE-VERIFY: open a Master rack in the flat elevation. Each device reads as a DARK tray with a thin colour stripe on its left edge - GPU cyan, switch violet, PDU and CDU gold, storage pink, server and CPU light blue, patch and media conv and unclassified grey - and the label stays readable on every one. If any block is a solid colour slab, .429 is still live and this ship did not take.
